items.title: Solar cost decline
items.claim: Utility-scale solar PV levelised cost of electricity (LCOE) fell by roughly how much between 2010 and 2022?
items.reveal:
IRENA's 2023 cost report found utility-scale solar PV LCOE fell from around $0.45/kWh in 2010 to $0.049/kWh in 2022 in real terms.

Wind and battery costs followed similar trajectories.
items.why: Technology learning curves can outpace policy timelines on energy transition.

items.title: Ocean pH change since pre-industrial
items.claim: Surface ocean pH has fallen since the late 18th century. By approximately how much?

options.text: About 0.1 units (around 30% rise in hydrogen ion concentration)

items.reveal:
Mean surface ocean pH has declined from around 8.2 to about 8.1 since pre-industrial times. The pH scale is logarithmic, so this is roughly a 26-30% rise in hydrogen ion concentration.

The IPCC SROCC (2019) projected further decline of 0.3-0.4 by 2100 under high-emission scenarios.
items.why: Small numbers on a log scale can correspond to large biological consequences.

items.title: Methane's GWP comparison
items.claim: Methane is a more potent greenhouse gas than CO2 over short timescales. Approximately how does its 100-year global warming potential compare?

options.text: Around 28-30 times CO2 over 100 years (IPCC AR6)

items.reveal_title: About 28-30x over 100 years; closer to 80x over 20 years
items.reveal:
IPCC AR6 reports GWP-100 of around 27-30 for fossil and biogenic methane. Methane's atmospheric lifetime is about 12 years, making it a strong near-term lever.

The Global Methane Pledge (2021) targets a 30% cut by 2030.
items.why: Choice of GWP averaging window shapes how big methane appears to be as a problem.
